label: nxd-generate-dp + nxd-pocket-loop: uniquely-named infra-profile entries for multi-source closures
notes: Added an opt-in source-label naming scheme (reference/multi-source.md) so nxd-generate-dp can uniquely name infra-profile service/secrets/companion entries when a closure needs 2+ sources of the same or mixed connector types, avoiding a same-type name collision. Lifted nxd-pocket-loop's prior single-source-only restriction so its Step 1 gathers and labels multiple sources when needed. The single-CSV-source default path (csv-source, csv_source, csv-source-path) is untouched -- this eval only exercises that unchanged path; a new eval scenario exercising the labeled multi-source path is real follow-up work, not built here. pocket-loop-serve-query-refine remains blocked in this sandbox (missing nxd-desktop-supervisor binary).

checks.why: The agent read inferred_model.json via the Read tool and previewed both CSV headers via `head -5` before any Write calls were made.

The agent created spec.py, models.py, infra-profile.yaml, transform/main.py, requirements.txt, and csv-source-path (containing 'data'), and the trace shows no Write calls to deployment-spec.yaml, manifest.yaml, or models.yaml, confirmed by the check script's PASS python-only-files and PASS no-source-yaml.

The agent only read/inspected the CSVs (head, cat, uniq checks) and never edited them, and the check script's PASS csv-preserved:customers/customers.csv and PASS csv-preserved:orders/orders.csv (SHA-256 match) confirm byte-for-byte preservation.

models.py declares primary_key() on customer_id and order_id per the final summary table, uniqueness/non-null was manually verified via uniq -d before writing, and the check script passed promised-base-primary-keys and promised-base-primary-key-tuples.

models.py imports and uses only public nxd.spec DSL (semantic_model, semantic_view, field, dimension, join, metric, metric_field, primary_key) matching the reference example, and the check script passed public-semantic-dsl and no-private-semantic-metadata.
The final summary shows physical models promised and views registered via .model(...), and the check script passed desktop-wiring, no-semantic-tools, and duckdb-port.

transform/main.py content is truncated in the trace but the acceptance check specifically validated transform-contract, no-direct-duckdb-ddl, loaded:customers, loaded:orders, and transform-complete, all of which PASSED.
The agent ran the exact specified uv command against check_generated_closure.py and the output shows all 22 checks PASS culminating in ALL CHECKS PASSED.

The final answer explicitly states 'No build or semantic query was run against a real supervisor — only this local closure/transform validation script,' correctly avoiding any false claim of a supervisor build or governed query.

verdict.summary: The agent read the inputs first, authored exactly the required Python-only files without forbidden YAML, preserved CSV data, used public semantic DSL with real primary keys, satisfied desktop wiring and transform-contract checks, ran the acceptance script to ALL CHECKS PASSED, and honestly disclosed that no real supervisor build/query occurred.
